question: A finance team runs an overnight batch of several thousand transaction narratives that must be finished before the six o'clock reporting cut-off. They move the batch to the deepest-reasoning tier because they want the best possible quality. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The team grows used to a higher standard of narrative and finds the earlier output unacceptable if they ever have to revert.
B) The narratives come back written in a more elaborate style than the reporting template was originally designed to accommodate.
C) The batch does not finish inside the overnight window, so the morning report goes out incomplete or does not go out at all.
D) The batch produces more detail per transaction than the finance team has time to read through before the reporting cut-off.
correct_answers: C) The batch does not finish inside the overnight window, so the morning report goes out incomplete or does not go out at all.
explanations: Raised expectations are a soft consequence and only matter if the team later reverts. They have no bearing on whether tonight's batch clears the six o'clock deadline.
An elaborate style is a formatting mismatch that can be corrected by asking for a tighter format. It does not threaten the report itself in the way a missed cut-off does.

Correct. At this volume the binding constraint is throughput against a fixed deadline. Depth that cannot complete in the window fails the task outright, which is worse than slightly plainer narratives delivered on time.
Excess detail costs reading time, but the narratives are generated per transaction and are not all read individually. The scheduling failure is the far more serious outcome here.
